thread:
maya: quick question for the hosting surface follow-up 1 
maya: in sidecarless private deployments how do we want auth to flow from control plane -> runtime when we can't inject secrets?
Tony: are we assuming the control plane lives in customer VPC and sidecars are disallowed by policy?
maya: yes, exactly that.
Olga: two patterns i keep circling: delegated short-lived tokens (control-plane issues runtime tokens) or runtime directly pulls from customer KMS via a provided adapter/proxy.
Liam: delegated tokens look simpler for hosted/dedicated but break for fully air-gapped on-prem where control-plane can't reach runtime.
Tony: for on-prem we probably need a pull model (runtime->customer-kms) or an explicit manual secret bootstrap at deploy time.
maya: how about hybrid: default to token-exchange for hosted/dedicated; for private/on-prem expose a "kms-pull" adapter with configurable poll cadence.
Olga: polling KMS on every request is a non-starter. we need local cache + rotation semantics, clear TTLs and a refresh state machine.
Liam: propose adapter behavior: initial fetch -> local cache with TTL -> background refresh when nearing TTL -> control-plane may push rotation hooks if network path exists.
Tony: +1. also standardize fail semantics: FAIL_OPEN vs FAIL_CLOSED for auth failures. customers expect deterministic behavior.
maya: default suggestions: private -> FAIL_CLOSED, hosted -> FAIL_OPEN (with telemetry/alerting). thoughts?
Olga: agree but document it prominently. also enforce a circuit-breaker: after N auth errors within window T, runtime should stop retries and return 503 with a structured error code.
Liam: sample error: {code: "AUTH_PROXY_UNAVAILABLE", mode: "private", details: "cache_stale"}  we'll publish exact schema.
maya: small config sketch for the hybrid adapter so we can iterate:
```
auth:
  mode: hybrid          # token-exchange | kms-pull | hybrid
  cache_ttl: 5m
  refresh_threshold: 30s
  fail_policy: closed   # open | closed
  rotation_webhook: https://hooks.customer.internal/rotate
```
Tony: operational notes: 1) telemetry: per-tenant metrics for token-exchange latency + failure_rate; surface in console. 2) RBAC: only org-admins can flip fail_policy.
Olga: + audit events for token issuance and rotation_webhook calls (include tenant id, request id, and who triggered).
Liam: i'll draft a tiny state machine for cache lifecycle: fresh -> expiring -> refresh_in_progress -> stale -> blocked. include backoff on refresh.
maya: action items: olga + liam to draft adapter API (kms-pull contract + cache semantics) by EOD Friday; tony to draft telemetry KPIs and thresholds; i'll update hosting-surface doc with FAIL_OPEN/CLOSED defaults and sample config.
infra-bot: deploy-check: no blocking issues found for the sketch. :white_check_mark:
Tony: ok. if no one objects i'll slot a 15m arch-sync agenda item Monday to review the adapter API.
Olga: ack, adding notes to the doc. if anyone thinks we missed a mode (e.g., manual-secrets) call it out here.
maya: manual secret bootstrap is an explicit opt-in fallback for air-gapped installs but should be last resort. document it as "operator-inserted" and require rotation TTLs.
Liam: also add a conformance test: simulate KMS unreachable + rotation webhook failing, assert fail_policy semantics and circuit-breaker behavior.
Tony: good point. tests should run in the integration harness for private mode validation.
maya: thanks all. i'll push the hosting surface update and link PR here once ready.
